17-1.title: Roman Achievements and Daily Life
17-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — ROMAN ACHIEVEMENTS AND DAILY LIFE

The Romans were MASTER BUILDERS and ENGINEERS. They built strong, long-lasting ROADS that connected the whole empire (giving us the saying 'all roads lead to Rome'). They built AQUEDUCTS, structures that carried fresh water over long distances into cities using gravity. They were among the first to use CONCRETE, which let them build huge structures like the Colosseum and domed buildings. They also developed strong systems of LAW that still shape legal ideas today.

Roman society was made up of different groups. PATRICIANS were the rich, upper-class families. PLEBEIANS were the common people, like farmers, workers, and craftspeople. There were also women, children, and many ENSLAVED people, who had very different and much harder daily lives. Each group's daily life was very different depending on their class.

Many things we use today come straight from Rome: our calendar, many words (Latin is the root of English words), styles of buildings and government, and important legal ideas. The Romans' achievements in engineering, building, and law are a big part of their lasting legacy. Remember: Rome = roads, aqueducts, concrete, and law.

17-2.title: The Fall of the Western Roman Empire
17-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE FALL OF THE WESTERN ROMAN EMPIRE

After the long peace of the Pax Romana ended, the Roman Empire began to face serious trouble. Over many years, the WESTERN half of the Roman Empire slowly DECLINED and grew weaker. The fall was not sudden; it happened gradually over a long time.

Historians point to several CAUSES that worked together. These included: WEAK and corrupt leaders (some emperors ruled badly), MONEY PROBLEMS (the economy struggled and the government ran out of money), the empire's HUGE SIZE (it became too big to defend and govern well), and INVASIONS by outside groups (often called barbarian tribes, like the Goths and Vandals) who attacked the borders. Disease and a shrinking army also played a part. No single cause brought Rome down; many problems combined.

Finally, in 476 AD, the last emperor of the Western Roman Empire was removed from power, and the Western Roman Empire had FALLEN. This event is often used to mark the END of the ancient classical world in Europe and the beginning of the Middle Ages. (The eastern half, the Byzantine Empire, lasted much longer.) Remember: the Western Roman Empire fell in 476 AD from many combined causes.

questions.question: What does it mean that 'no single cause' brought Rome down?

questions.question: The term 'barbarian tribes' in the lesson refers to which groups?

questions.question: Why is it WRONG to say Rome fell because of one emperor alone?

questions.question: After the Pax Romana ended, what began to happen to the Roman Empire?

questions.question: Which best explains why the fall is called a 'gradual' decline?

questions.question: Which group of people attacked Rome's borders?

choices.B: Outside tribes such as the Goths

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the two halves of the Roman Empire?

choices.C: The Western half fell in 476 AD, but the Eastern half lasted much longer

17-3.title: The Lasting Legacy of the Ancient World
17-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE LASTING LEGACY OF THE ANCIENT WORLD

Even after Rome fell, the great IDEAS of the ancient civilizations LIVED ON. A 'legacy' is something handed down from the past that still affects us today. The ancient world left behind an amazing legacy that we still use.

Think of all the gifts: from GREECE came DEMOCRACY (rule by the people), philosophy, and the Olympics. From ROME came LAW, republican government, roads, and engineering. From the ISRAELITES (Judaism) came MONOTHEISM, which shaped Christianity and Islam too. From the PHOENICIANS came the ALPHABET. From SUMER and EGYPT came WRITING (cuneiform and hieroglyphics) and early MATH and science. From INDIA and the MAYA came the concept of ZERO. From CHINA came inventions like paper and the compass.

Studying ancient civilizations is not just about the past — it helps us understand the ROOTS of the modern world we live in today. Our governments, writing, math, religions, calendars, and buildings all grew from seeds planted by these early peoples. The ancient world's legacy is all around us. Remember: democracy = Greece; law = Rome; alphabet = Phoenicia; monotheism = Israelites; writing = Sumer/Egypt.

questions.question: Which legacy came from ancient ROME?

questions.question: The idea of monotheism is part of the legacy of which people?

questions.question: The alphabet is part of the legacy of which people?

questions.question: Which two civilizations gave us early WRITING systems?
questions.explanation: Sumer's cuneiform and Egypt's hieroglyphics were early writing.

questions.question: Why is studying ancient civilizations useful today?

choices.A: It has no use at all
choices.B: It helps us understand the roots of the modern world
choices.C: It only teaches us about rivers

questions.explanation: Studying the ancient world reveals the roots of modern life.

questions.question: Which invention is part of the legacy of ancient CHINA?
questions.explanation: Paper and the compass were Chinese inventions.

questions.question: Which two faraway civilizations both contributed the concept of ZERO?
questions.explanation: Both India and the Maya developed the concept of zero.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the legacy of the ancient world?

choices.A: The ancient world has no connection to today
choices.B: Nothing from the ancient world survived
choices.C: Our governments, writing, math, and religions grew from these early peoples

questions.explanation: Modern governments, writing, math, and religions all trace to the ancient world.

questions.question: Which gift came from ancient Greece?
questions.explanation: Philosophy and the Olympics were part of the Greek legacy.

questions.question: The concept of ZERO came from which two civilizations?
questions.explanation: Both India and the Maya developed the concept of zero.

questions.question: Which civilization gave us cuneiform writing?
questions.explanation: Sumer gave us cuneiform, one of the earliest forms of writing.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a legacy of the ancient world described in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Democracy, law, and the alphabet were ancient legacies; television was not.

questions.question: Christianity and Islam were both shaped by which idea handed down from the Israelites?
questions.explanation: Monotheism, from the Israelites, helped shape Christianity and Islam.

questions.question: Which civilization is correctly matched with its legacy?
questions.explanation: Democracy is correctly matched with ancient Greece.

questions.question: If you trace the letters of the English alphabet back to the ancient world, which people should you thank?
questions.explanation: The Phoenicians created the alphabet that influenced later writing.

questions.question: Hieroglyphics, an early writing system, came from which civilization?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphics were an early form of writing from Egypt.

questions.question: Why does the lesson say studying ancient civilizations is useful?

choices.B: It helps us understand the roots of the modern world
choices.C: It has nothing to do with today

questions.explanation: Studying ancient civilizations helps us understand the roots of the modern world.

questions.question: The word 'democracy' means rule by the _____.
questions.explanation: Democracy, a Greek legacy, means rule by the people.

questions.question: Roads and engineering are part of the legacy of which civilization?
questions.explanation: Roads and engineering were Roman legacies.

questions.question: Which BEST explains why ancient legacies still matter today?

choices.A: Our governments, writing, math, and religions grew from them
choices.D: They have no effect on modern life

questions.explanation: Modern governments, writing, math, and religions grew from ancient legacies.

questions.question: Paper, a useful invention we still use, was part of the legacy of which civilization?
questions.explanation: Paper was a Chinese invention handed down to the world.

questions.question: Which statement compares the legacies of Greece and Rome correctly?

choices.A: Greece gave law; Rome gave democracy
choices.B: Greece gave the alphabet; Rome gave zero
choices.C: Greece gave democracy; Rome gave law and engineering

questions.explanation: Greece gave democracy, while Rome gave law and engineering.

questions.question: A country today that lets its citizens vote for leaders is using an idea rooted in which civilization?
questions.explanation: Voting for leaders comes from the Greek idea of democracy.

questions.question: Which group of inventions all came from CHINA?
questions.explanation: Paper and the compass both came from China.

questions.question: Which of these is the BEST definition of 'monotheism'?
questions.explanation: Monotheism, from the Israelites, is the belief in one God.

questions.question: Early math and science were part of the legacy of which civilizations?
questions.explanation: Sumer and Egypt contributed early math and science.

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of using an ancient legacy in daily life today?

choices.A: Writing a note using letters from the alphabet
choices.B: Inventing something with no past at all

questions.explanation: Writing with the alphabet, a Phoenician legacy, is using an ancient legacy daily.

questions.question: Which civilization is INCORRECTLY matched with its legacy?
questions.explanation: The alphabet came from Phoenicia, not China, so that match is incorrect.

questions.question: Why did the great IDEAS of ancient civilizations 'live on' even after Rome fell?

choices.A: They were passed down and still affect us today

questions.explanation: The ideas lived on because they were passed down and still affect us today.

questions.question: Judaism, the religion of the Israelites, is best known for introducing which idea?

questions.question: Which list correctly matches gifts to the civilizations that gave them?
questions.explanation: Democracy came from Greece, law from Rome, and the alphabet from Phoenicia.

questions.question: The Olympics that countries hold today grew from a tradition of which civilization?
questions.explanation: The Olympics came from ancient Greece.

questions.question: Republican government, where representatives are chosen, is most connected to which civilization's legacy?
questions.explanation: Republican government is part of the Roman legacy.

questions.question: Which sentence about the legacy of the ancient world is TRUE?

questions.question: Which pair shows a civilization and a gift it did NOT give?

choices.B: Ideas from ancient civilizations still shape our world today
